```{python}
import geopandas as gpd
from shapely.geometry import box

xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax = 541000, 5210000, 565000, 5238000
study = gpd.GeoDataFrame({"name": ["Lower Puyallup valley"]},
                         geometry=[box(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)], crs=26910)
print(f"{(xmax - xmin) / 1000:.0f} km wide x {(ymax - ymin) / 1000:.0f} km tall")

study.to_crs(4326).to_file("data/reach/valley_extent.geojson", driver="GeoJSON")

                  tiles="Esri.WorldImagery")
m.save("valley_extent_map.html")
```

## Step 2: download the elevation tiles

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import requests

base = "https://prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com/StagedProducts/Elevation/1m/Projects"
downloads = {
    ("WA_PierceCounty_2020_A20", "data/raw/usgs_dem2020"):
        ["x54y522", "x54y523", "x54y524", "x55y522", "x55y523", "x55y524",
         "x56y522", "x56y523", "x56y524"],
    ("WA_KingCounty_2021_B21", "data/raw/usgs_dem2021_king"):
        ["x54y524", "x55y523", "x55y524", "x56y523", "x56y524"],
}

for (project, folder), tiles in downloads.items():
    out_dir = Path(folder)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for t in tiles:
        name = f"USGS_1M_10_{t}_{project}.tif"
        dest = out_dir / name
        if dest.exists():
            print("already have", name)
            continue
        print("downloading", name, "...")
        url = f"{base}/{project}/TIFF/{name}"
        tmp = dest.with_suffix(".part")
        with requests.get(url, stream=True, timeout=120) as r:
            r.raise_for_status()
            with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
                for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=1024 * 1024):
                    f.write(chunk)
        tmp.replace(dest)
        print("  done")
```

---
## Step 3: mosaic the 14 tiles into one 3 m DEM

```{python}
import rasterio
from rasterio.merge import merge
from rasterio.enums import Resampling

pierce = sorted(Path("data/raw/usgs_dem2020").glob("*.tif"))
king = sorted(Path("data/raw/usgs_dem2021_king").glob("*.tif"))
files = pierce + king      # Pierce first, so Pierce wins where both have data

srcs = [rasterio.open(f) for f in files]
mosaic, transform = merge(srcs, bounds=(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax), res=3,
                          resampling=Resampling.average, method="first")
profile = srcs[0].profile
for s in srcs:
    s.close()

profile.update(height=mosaic.shape[1], width=mosaic.shape[2], transform=transform,
               compress="deflate", tiled=True, blockxsize=512, blockysize=512,
               BIGTIFF="IF_SAFER")
with rasterio.open("data/processed/valley_dem_3m.tif", "w", **profile) as dst:
    dst.write(mosaic.astype("float32"))

print(mosaic.shape)
```
```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

dem = np.where(mosaic[0] == profile["nodata"], np.nan, mosaic[0])
print(f"elevation {np.nanmin(dem):.1f} to {np.nanmax(dem):.1f} m, "
      f"{np.isnan(dem).mean() * 100:.2f}% no data")

plt.figure(figsize=(6, 7))
plt.imshow(dem[::4, ::4], cmap="terrain")
plt.colorbar(label="elevation (m)")
plt.title("Lower Puyallup valley DEM, 3 m")
```

## Step 4: get the three river lines

```{python}
import pandas as pd

lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max = study.to_crs(4326).total_bounds

url = "https://hydro.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nhd/MapServer/6/query"
params = {
    "where": "GNIS_NAME IN ('Puyallup River','Carbon River','White River')",
    "geometry": f"{lon_min},{lat_min},{lon_max},{lat_max}",
    "geometryType": "esriGeometryEnvelope",
    "inSR": 4326,
    "outFields": "GNIS_NAME",
    "outSR": 4326,
    "f": "geojson",
}
r = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=60)
r.raise_for_status()
flow = gpd.GeoDataFrame.from_features(r.json()["features"], crs=4326)

# the last stretch of the Puyallup to Commencement Bay has no name in NHD
params_mouth = dict(params,
                    where="FTYPE=558 AND GNIS_NAME IS NULL",
                    geometry="-122.42,47.238,-122.40,47.252")
r2 = requests.get(url, params=params_mouth, timeout=60)
r2.raise_for_status()
mouth = gpd.GeoDataFrame.from_features(r2.json()["features"], crs=4326)
mouth["gnis_name"] = "Puyallup River"

flow = pd.concat([flow, mouth], ignore_index=True)
flow = flow.to_crs(26910).clip(study).explode(index_parts=False)
flow.to_file("data/reach/valley_rivers.geojson", driver="GeoJSON")

flow["length_km"] = flow.length / 1000
flow.groupby("gnis_name")["length_km"].sum().round(1)
```
```{python}
left, top = transform.c, transform.f
extent = (left, left + 3 * mosaic.shape[2], top - 3 * mosaic.shape[1], top)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 7))
ax.imshow(dem[::4, ::4], cmap="terrain", extent=extent)
flow.plot(ax=ax, column="gnis_name", legend=True, linewidth=1, cmap="autumn")
ax.set_title("River lines over the valley DEM")
```

## Step 5: the valley REM

```{python}
from rasterio.transform import rowcol

def low_point(x, y, half=5):
    row, col = rowcol(transform, x, y)
    win = dem[max(row - half, 0):row + half + 1, max(col - half, 0):col + half + 1]
    if win.size == 0 or np.all(np.isnan(win)):
        return np.nan
    return np.nanpercentile(win, 5)

rows = []
for name, line in zip(flow.gnis_name, flow.geometry):
    for d in np.arange(0, line.length, 25):
        p = line.interpolate(d)
        rows.append({"river": name, "x": p.x, "y": p.y, "z": low_point(p.x, p.y)})

pts = pd.DataFrame(rows).dropna()
pts.groupby("river").z.describe()
```

---
## 5b. Build the water surface and the REM

```{python}
from rasterio.transform import Affine
from rasterio.warp import reproject, Resampling
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter

tree = cKDTree(pts[["x", "y"]].values)
z_river = pts["z"].values

# water surface on a coarse grid: 10 cells = 30 m
step = 10
ch, cw = int(np.ceil(dem.shape[0] / step)), int(np.ceil(dem.shape[1] / step))
coarse_t = transform * Affine.scale(step)
cx = coarse_t.c + (np.arange(cw) + 0.5) * coarse_t.a
cy = coarse_t.f + (np.arange(ch) + 0.5) * coarse_t.e
X, Y = np.meshgrid(cx, cy)

dist, idx = tree.query(np.column_stack([X.ravel(), Y.ravel()]), k=48)
w = 1 / np.maximum(dist, 1) ** 2
ws_coarse = (np.sum(w * z_river[idx], axis=1) / np.sum(w, axis=1)).reshape(ch, cw)
ws_coarse = gaussian_filter(ws_coarse, sigma=5)

# back to 3 m, then subtract
ws = np.empty_like(dem)
reproject(ws_coarse.astype("float32"), ws,
          src_transform=coarse_t, dst_transform=transform,
          src_crs=profile["crs"], dst_crs=profile["crs"],
          resampling=Resampling.bilinear)
rem = dem - ws

rem_profile = profile.copy()
rem_profile.update(dtype="float32", nodata=np.nan)
with rasterio.open("data/processed/rem_valley_3m.tif", "w", **rem_profile) as dst:
    dst.write(rem.astype("float32"), 1)

np.nanpercentile(rem, [1, 10, 25, 50, 75]).round(2)
```

### ~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Step 3b: fill the gaps ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

```{python}
ned_url = ("https://prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com/StagedProducts/Elevation/13/"
           "TIFF/current/n48w123/USGS_13_n48w123.tif")
ned_path = Path("data/raw/usgs_ned_13/USGS_13_n48w123.tif")
ned_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

if not ned_path.exists():
    print("downloading 10 m DEM ...")
    tmp = ned_path.with_suffix(".part")
    with requests.get(ned_url, stream=True, timeout=120) as r:
        r.raise_for_status()
        with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
            for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=1024 * 1024):
                f.write(chunk)
    tmp.replace(ned_path)

# put the 10 m DEM on our exact 3 m grid
with rasterio.open(ned_path) as src:
    ned = np.full(dem.shape, np.nan, dtype="float32")
    reproject(rasterio.band(src, 1), ned,
              dst_transform=transform, dst_crs=profile["crs"],
              resampling=Resampling.bilinear, dst_nodata=np.nan)

# fill only the holes
gaps = np.isnan(dem)
dem_filled = np.where(gaps, ned, dem).astype("float32")

# make the filled bay match the bay water level in the 1 m data
bay_level = np.nanmedian(dem[dem < 0.5])
bay_gap = gaps & (ned < 1)
dem_filled[bay_gap] = bay_level
print(f"bay water set to {bay_level:.2f} m")

print(f"filled {gaps.mean() * 100:.2f}% of the map, "
      f"{np.isnan(dem_filled).mean() * 100:.2f}% still empty")

# save, and rebuild the REM with the filled DEM
with rasterio.open("data/processed/valley_dem_3m_filled.tif", "w",
                   **dict(profile, nodata=np.nan)) as dst:
    dst.write(dem_filled, 1)

rem = dem_filled - ws
with rasterio.open("data/processed/rem_valley_3m.tif", "w", **rem_profile) as dst:
    dst.write(rem.astype("float32"), 1)
```

### ~~~~~~~ 3c. Seafloor for Commencement Bay (NOAA topobathy) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import requests
import numpy as np
import rasterio
from rasterio.warp import reproject, Resampling

bathy_dir = Path("data/raw/noaa_cudem")
bathy_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
base = ("https://chs.coast.noaa.gov/htdata/raster2/elevation/"
        "NCEI_ninth_Topobathy_2014_8483/wash_pugetsound/")
names = ["ncei19_n47x50_w122x50_2023v1.tif",   # 47.25-47.50 N: most of the bay
         "ncei19_n47x25_w122x50_2024v1.tif"]   # 47.00-47.25 N: the south end of the waterways

for name in names:
    out = bathy_dir / name
    if out.exists():
        print("already have", name)
        continue
    part = out.with_suffix(".part")
    with requests.get(base + name, stream=True, timeout=120) as r:
        r.raise_for_status()
        with open(part, "wb") as f:
            for chunk in r.iter_content(1 << 20):
                f.write(chunk)
    part.rename(out)
    print("downloaded", name)

# put the NOAA tiles onto our 3 m grid
with rasterio.open("data/processed/valley_dem_3m_filled.tif") as src:
    land = src.read(1)
    prof = src.profile

bathy = np.full(land.shape, np.nan, dtype="float32")
for name in names:
    with rasterio.open(bathy_dir / name) as src:
        piece = np.full(land.shape, np.nan, dtype="float32")
        reproject(rasterio.band(src, 1), piece, src_nodata=src.nodata,
                  dst_transform=prof["transform"], dst_crs=prof["crs"], dst_nodata=np.nan,
                  resampling=Resampling.bilinear)
    bathy = np.where(np.isnan(bathy), piece, bathy)

# keep only cells that are flat water in our DEM and below sea level in NOAA's
water = (land < 0.5) & (bathy < 0)
seafloor = np.where(water, bathy, np.nan).astype("float32")
print(f"seafloor cells: {water.sum():,}")
print(f"depth range: {np.nanmin(seafloor):.0f} m to {np.nanmax(seafloor):.1f} m")

p = prof.copy()
p.update(dtype="float32", nodata=np.nan, compress="deflate", predictor=3, tiled=True)
with rasterio.open("data/processed/valley_seafloor_3m.tif", "w", **p) as dst:
    dst.write(seafloor, 1)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 6))
im = ax.imshow(seafloor, cmap="viridis")
ax.set_xlim(0, 3500); ax.set_ylim(3500, 0)   # zoom to the bay corner
plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="Depth (m, NAVD88)")
ax.set_title("Commencement Bay seafloor (NOAA CUDEM)")
plt.show()
```

### 6a. Layers

```{python}
import gc
import logging
import numpy as np
import rasterio
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patheffects as pe
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap, to_rgb
from rasterio import features
from scipy import ndimage
from pyproj import Transformer
from PIL import Image

CELL = 3  # full 3 m detail

def read_band(path):
    with rasterio.open(path) as src:
        return src.read(1).astype("float32"), src.transform

rem_map, tf = read_band("data/processed/rem_valley_3m.tif")
dem_map, _ = read_band("data/processed/valley_dem_3m_filled.tif")
H, W = rem_map.shape
ext = (tf.c, tf.c + W * tf.a, tf.f + H * tf.e, tf.f)

# valley floor = low ground (< 15 m above the river) connected to one of the rivers
rivers = gpd.read_file("data/reach/valley_rivers.geojson").to_crs(26910)
river_px = features.rasterize(((g, 1) for g in rivers.geometry), out_shape=(H, W),
                              transform=tf, all_touched=True).astype(bool)
low = rem_map < 15
labels, n = ndimage.label(low)
keep = np.unique(labels[river_px & low])
valley = np.isin(labels, keep[keep > 0])
del labels, low, river_px
print(f"valley floor: {valley.mean() * 100:.1f}% of the map")

# seafloor: keep the open bay and the waterways joined to it (drops stray river bits)
seafloor, _ = read_band("data/processed/valley_seafloor_3m.tif")
sea_lab, _ = ndimage.label(~np.isnan(seafloor))
sizes = np.bincount(sea_lab.ravel())
sizes[0] = 0
sea = sea_lab == sizes.argmax()
del sea_lab
print(f"seafloor: {sea.sum() * CELL * CELL / 1e6:.1f} km2, down to {np.nanmin(seafloor[sea]):.0f} m")
```

### 6b. Colors, relief and glow

```{python}
stops = ["#f7fcfd", "#d3ecf2", "#86c1d1", "#2e7594", "#123d5d", "#081b2c"]
deep = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("deep", stops)
BG, TEXT, SUB = "#081b2c", "#e8f3f6", "#9dbfcc"

RMAX, K = 10.0, 0.8   # colors fade out by 10 m; K sets how fast (smaller = faster)
val = np.where(valley, np.clip(rem_map, 0, RMAX), RMAX).astype("float32")
t = (np.log1p(val / K) / np.log1p(RMAX / K)).astype("float32")   # 0 = river level, 1 = 10 m or more
del val

# color through a lookup table (much lighter on memory than deep(t))
lut = deep(np.linspace(0, 1, 1024))[:, :3].astype("float32")
rgb = lut[(t * 1023).astype("uint16")]

# the bay and port waterways (the river keeps its REM colors all the way to its mouth)
water = sea

# the bay gets its own gradient: light where shallow (the delta), dark where deep
sea_stops = ["#8cc4d3", "#3f86a2", "#1a4d6a", "#0b2236"]
sea_cmap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("sea", sea_stops)
DEPTH_MAX = 150.0
d = (np.clip(-seafloor[sea], 0, DEPTH_MAX) / DEPTH_MAX) ** 0.6   # spreads out the shallow end
rgb[sea] = sea_cmap(d)[:, :3]
del d

# shade from one surface: land from the lidar DEM, the bay from the NOAA seafloor
relief = np.where(sea, seafloor, dem_map)
VEX = 4.0                                        # vertical exaggeration (higher = more relief)

def hillshade(z, azdeg, altdeg):
    """Same math as matplotlib's LightSource.hillshade, but in float32 so it fits in memory."""
    gy, gx = np.gradient(z * np.float32(VEX), np.float32(-CELL), np.float32(CELL))
    az, alt = np.radians(90 - azdeg), np.radians(altdeg)
    lx, ly, lz = np.cos(az) * np.cos(alt), np.sin(az) * np.cos(alt), np.sin(alt)
    hs = (-gx * lx - gy * ly + lz) / np.sqrt(gx * gx + gy * gy + 1)
    del gx, gy
    lo, hi = np.nanpercentile(hs, [0.1, 99.9])
    return np.clip((hs - lo) / (hi - lo), 0, 1).astype("float32")

hs = 0.75 * hillshade(relief, 315, 35) + 0.25 * hillshade(relief, 225, 50)   # main NW light + soft SW fill
edge = ndimage.gaussian_filter(valley.astype("float32"), sigma=15)   # 0 uplands, 1 valley, feathered between
strength = 0.70 - 0.30 * edge                    # 0.40 on the valley floor, 0.70 on the uplands
strength[sea] = 0.75                             # strong relief on the seafloor
shade = 1 - strength * (1 - hs)
rgb *= shade[..., None]

# lift sunlit slopes so relief shows even on the near-black uplands and in the bay
LIFT = 0.16                                      # higher = brighter ridges
sun = np.clip(hs - 0.55, 0, None) * (LIFT * (1 - 0.6 * edge))
sun[sea] = np.clip(hs[sea] - 0.55, 0, None) * LIFT * 1.5
for i, c in enumerate(to_rgb(stops[2])):
    rgb[..., i] += sun * c
del hs, edge, strength, shade, sun, relief

# glow around the river
glow = ndimage.gaussian_filter((1 - t) * (valley & ~water), sigma=20)   # 20 cells x 3 m = 60 m
del t
gcol = np.array(to_rgb(stops[1]), dtype="float32")
for i in range(3):                                   # screen blend, one color band at a time
    rgb[..., i] = 1 - (1 - rgb[..., i]) * (1 - 0.30 * glow * gcol[i])
del glow
np.clip(rgb, 0, 1, out=rgb)

# shrink the 3 m picture to exactly 4K wide with a sharp Lanczos filter
PX_W, PX_H = 5120, 5973   # sharp enough for close zooms on the story page
img = np.asarray(Image.fromarray((rgb * 255).round().astype("uint8")).resize((PX_W, PX_H), Image.LANCZOS))
del rgb
gc.collect()
```

```{python}
# bay label

ax.text(x, y, "Commencement\nBay", color=TEXT, fontsize=11, fontfamily=SERIF, style="italic",
        ha="center", va="center", path_effects=halo)

# scale bar

sy = ext[2] + 0.075 * (ext[3] - ext[2])
ax.plot([sx, sx + 5000], [sy, sy], color=SUB, lw=2)
ax.text(sx + 2500, sy + 350, "5 km", color=SUB, fontsize=9, fontfamily=SANS, ha="center")

# north arrow beside the scale bar: arrow on top, N underneath
nx, ny = sx + 7500, sy - 300
ax.annotate("", xy=(nx, ny + 1700), xytext=(nx, ny + 300),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>,head_width=0.35,head_length=0.7", color=TEXT, lw=1.5))
ax.text(nx, ny, "N", color=TEXT, fontsize=13, fontfamily=SERIF, ha="center", va="top", path_effects=halo)

# credits
fig.text(0.058, 0.022, "Data: USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM (Pierce 2020, King 2021), NOAA NCEI CUDEM topobathy, "
         "USGS NHD. Method after Daniel Coe (IDW REM). Map: Jordan, 2026.",
         color=SUB, fontsize=7.5, fontfamily=SANS, alpha=0.8)

fig.savefig("figures/valley_rem_4k.png", dpi=320, facecolor=BG)   # 3840 x 4480
fig.savefig("figures/valley_rem_web.png", dpi=110, facecolor=BG)  # website version
```

### 6d. Clean map for the story page

```{python}
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12, 14), facecolor=BG)
ax = fig.add_axes([0, 0, 1, 1])
ax.imshow(img, extent=ext, interpolation="none")
ax.set_xlim(ext[0], ext[1])
ax.set_ylim(ext[2], ext[3])
ax.axis("off")
for name, (lon, lat) in towns.items():
    x, y = to_utm.transform(lon, lat)
    ax.text(x, y, name.upper(), color=TEXT, fontsize=10, fontfamily=SANS,
            ha="center", va="center", path_effects=halo)
for name, (lon, lat, angle) in river_names.items():
    x, y = to_utm.transform(lon, lat)
    ax.text(x, y, name, color=TEXT, fontsize=11, fontfamily=SERIF, style="italic",
            rotation=angle, ha="center", va="center", path_effects=halo)
x, y = to_utm.transform(-122.433, 47.279)
ax.text(x, y, "Commencement\nBay", color=TEXT, fontsize=12, fontfamily=SERIF, style="italic",
        ha="center", va="center", path_effects=halo)
fig.savefig("figures/valley_story.jpg", dpi=PX_W / 12, facecolor=BG, pil_kwargs={"quality": 88})   # 5120 px wide
plt.close(fig)
```
